text:
maya: Heads-up — following the offload RFC I prototyped a small lifecycle state machine for VM-backed allocations. Wanted quick feedback on edge cases we might have missed.

alex: nice. can you paste the state diagram?

maya: sure — simplified: INIT -> ACTIVE -> STAGED -> EVICTED -> RECLAIMED. transitions: ACTIVE->STAGED on idle hint, STAGED->EVICTED if pressure or timeout, EVICTED->RECLAIMED when host freed.

ben: what's the difference between STAGED and EVICTED in practice? seems like duplication.

maya: STAGED keeps a lightweight host mapping (pinned page metadata, small IO buffer) so reconnect is fast. EVICTED drops host mapping and requires async fetch. STAGED is cheaper to keep but increases fragmentation risk.

sam: question: how do we account for NUMA locality when moving to STAGED? if we stage to remote node memory we can blow latency.

maya: good point. current proto tags staged entries with preferred NUMA node and a fallback. admission checks refuse staging to remote if latency budget < X ms.

lee: can we encode that policy as simple thresholds? history shows thresholds get brittle. maybe a score combining bandwidth, latency, and page hotness.

alex: +1 to score. also need to expose telemetry so SREs can tune without code changes. e.g., staged_count_by_node, avg_reconnect_ms, staged_eviction_rate. offload-bot: telemetry task created #4571

ben: how do we avoid fragmentation from many small staged allocations? coalesce on reclaim? free list compaction?

maya: prototype does periodic coalesce pass that merges adjacent staged ranges if they belong to same tenant and contiguous vaddr. it's cheap because staged ranges track original allocation IDs. downside: coalesce needs a barrier to avoid racing reconnects.

sam: barrier sounds risky during high qps. can coalesce be opportunistic during reclaim when qps is low?

maya: yes — plan: opportunistic coalesce with soft-locks, and full compaction run only during maintenance windows or when fragmentation metric > threshold.

lee: what about prioritizing keeps for very hot KV-cache-like slices? we need a 'pin' hint that beats staging.

maya: added pin hint in the API: callers can provide keep_priority: high|normal|low. Pin prevents staging unless forced by OOM.

alex: API backwards compatibility: default keep_priority should be normal. Also add per-tenant quotas for pinned bytes to avoid abuse.

ben: eviction order: do we prefer evicting STAGED over ACTIVE or vice versa?

maya: current policy: prefer STAGED (cheap to drop) unless its expected reconnect cost > benefit (score). we compute reconnect_cost = avg_reconnect_ms * token_cost_factor, compare to save_cost = bytes_saved * cost_per_byte.

sam: might be worth running small sim to calibrate those weights. can we replay trace from last month? offload-bot: trace-replay job queued (id: tr-2026-03-18-08)

lee: also ensure we don't thrash: track recent reconnects per allocation and add cooldown windows to avoid repeated evict/reconnect loops.

maya: implemented cooldown in prototype; default 30s per allocation. open question: should cooldown be tenant-weighted?

alex: tenant-weighted makes sense for fairness, but need a simple config. OK status: prototype ready for bench, will post perf numbers.

ben: one more — heap snapshots for debugging fragmentation would be huge help. even a sparse index of staged ranges per tenant.

maya: agreed. adding a /debug/allocations endpoint that returns summarized staged map. will limit locks.

sam: fine. if you want I can pair on the trace replay and sims tomorrow.

maya: thanks — pairing would help. I'll merge proto into feature branch after adding telemetry. offload-bot: merged branch maya/unified-vmem-proto -> feature/offload-proto (CI passed) :tada:

lee: awesome. follow-up items: 1) telemetry dashboards 2) trace sim runs 3) tenant pin quotas 4) compaction config. I'll open issues.

maya: thanks all. closing for now, will circle back with numbers.
